inline_comments.comment:
`variant.effort` is cast to `'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'max'` with `as`, but this is the exact definition of `ClaudeEffort`. Since `execute` is called via `AgentDriver.execute` which receives an `AgentVariant`, the caller should have already narrowed to a claude variant. The cast hides the fact that `variant` here isn't narrowed to `{ agent: 'claude' }`. Consider typing the parameter or narrowing before use:

```typescript
if (variant.agent !== 'claude') throw new Error('...');
const effort = variant.effort; // now typed as ClaudeEffort
```

`git add -A` stages every untracked and modified file in `repoRoot` before computing the diff. The comment says "Safe: this runs on an ephemeral trial copy" but there is no programmatic guard enforcing that. If `getChangedFiles` were ever called with a path that isn't a trial copy (e.g. during a test or if trial directory resolution has a bug), it would silently stage everything in that repo. Consider either asserting that `repoRoot` is under `TRIALS_DIR` before running this command, or using `git diff HEAD --name-status` for tracked files and a separate untracked-file walk for new files.

Two related problems with the cache:

1. **Race condition**: if `eval-parallel.ts` spawns several processes for the same project simultaneously and none of them find `cacheDir/.git` yet, all will try to clone and populate the cache concurrently, potentially corrupting it. A simple file-based lock (or checking for a `.lock` sentinel and waiting) would prevent this.

2. **No invalidation**: the cache is populated once and never refreshed. If the `eval-baseline` branch is updated upstream, stale clones will be used indefinitely. Consider storing the remote HEAD SHA in the cache and comparing it on each run, or documenting a manual `--refresh-cache` flag.

If `git clone` or `installDeps` throws, the partially-created `repoRoot` and `trialDir` are left on disk. On the next run the cache check at line 33 will still be false (no `.git` in `cacheDir`), so a fresh clone will be attempted, but the stale `trialDir` may cause `mkdir` to silently succeed over garbage. Wrapping the else-branch in a try/finally that removes `trialDir` and `cacheDir` on failure would keep state consistent.

`ALL_EFFORTS` (line 13) and `ALL_MODELS` (line 9) are exported but not imported anywhere in the eval harness. If they are intended for future use, a comment saying so would clarify intent; otherwise remove them to keep the public surface minimal.

`promptName || 'setup'` appears twice (lines 47 and 76). Since `TrialConfig.prompt` is typed `string` (not optional) and the Zod schema already defaults it to `'setup'` before `runTrial` is called, an empty string reaching here would be a bug at the call site rather than a valid case to default away from. Remove the fallbacks and rely on the schema default, or validate `promptName` explicitly at the top of `runTrial`.

`citty` is added as a dependency but is not imported anywhere in the eval scripts (which use `node:util parseArgs` directly) or in any other file in the diff. If it was meant to replace `parseArgs` in `eval.ts`, the migration was not completed. If it's genuinely not needed, remove it to keep the dependency tree lean.

`getComponentCandidates` and `runGhostStories` are implementation details of the ghost-stories feature being promoted to the `storybook/internal/core-server` barrel export so the eval harness can import them. This creates a maintenance obligation: future changes to the ghost-stories internals must maintain backward compatibility with the eval harness interface. Consider whether the eval harness could instead import these directly via a relative path from `scripts/`, or whether a dedicated eval-specific export path would be cleaner than mixing them into the core-server public API.

The Codex agent has no equivalent to the Claude agent's `MAX_TURNS = 50` guard. If the Codex SDK does not enforce its own turn limit, a runaway session could iterate indefinitely and incur unbounded cost. Check whether `Codex.startThread` accepts a `maxTurns` or similar option and set it explicitly, matching the Claude agent's safety boundary.

general_comments.comment: **`eval-parallel.ts` is missing.** The PR description prominently describes it as the primary entry point for running all 8 model×prompt combinations with prefixed live-streamed logs, and the PR title positions the eval harness as a complete system. Only `eval.ts` (single run) is present in the diff. Either `eval-parallel.ts` was accidentally left out of this PR, or the description is ahead of the implementation — either way the discrepancy should be resolved before merging.

**`.agents/skills/review-pr/SKILL.md` is unrelated to this PR.** This new file (439 lines) is a skill definition for generating scrollable HTML PR review pages — it has nothing to do with the eval harness for Storybook setup. It appears to have been accidentally staged alongside the eval work. It should be moved to a separate PR or commit.

**Google Sheets upload is described but not implemented.** The PR description lists "Google Sheets upload (set `EVAL_GOOGLE_SHEETS_URL`)" as a results feature. No Google Sheets client code exists in the diff. If this is intentionally deferred, a `TODO` comment in `run-trial.ts` (where the report is assembled) and a note in the PR description would set accurate expectations.

**No overall trial budget or wall-clock timeout.** Individual steps have timeouts (build: 300s, tsc: 120s, clone: 120s, install: 300s), but the agent execution phase (`driver.execute`) is unbounded. A slow or hung agent will block the process indefinitely. Consider adding a top-level `Promise.race` with a configurable timeout in `runTrial`, or propagating a `--timeout` CLI flag through to the agent drivers.
